To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed energy-efficient scheduling and control schemes can reduce the total energy consumption in a TDMA/CDMAC WSN by 30%-50%, depending on network size and traffic load.
the energy efficiency of a hybrid TDMA-CDMA WSN is improved significantly by the joint optimization of adaptive power/rate controls and time-domain scheduling.

1) the energy efficiency of the interfering-cluster scheduling is limited; 2) the energy efficiency obtained with the proposed node scheduling heuristic algorithm is comparable to that of the optimal scheduling; and 3) the proposed PTC-UT/PTC-USG schemes provide comparable energy efficiency with PTC-IPT but with significantly lower complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy efficiency of hybrid TDMA/ CDMA WSNs and the corresponding algorithms for power/rate control as well as scheduling.
the fundamental problem of energy efficiency improvement for WSNs.
energy-efficient scheduling and control in hybrid TDMA-CDMA wireless sensor networking, which can be used in various WSN applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adaptive power/rate and scheduling control can provide significant energy saving in hybrid TDMA-CDMA wireless sensor networking.
adaptive power/rate controls combined with the proposed scheduling and PTC algorithms can provide significant energy efficiency improvement in a TDMA/CDMAs WSN.
the energy efficiency of the hybrid TDMA/ CDMA WSN is significantly improved by the joint use of adaptive power/rate and time-domain scheduling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a hybrid TDMA-CDMA WSN, adaptive transmission powers and times are the key to achieve energy-efficient power/rate scheduling.
the combination of the proposed adaptive power/rate and scheduling schemes is very effective in achieving the best energy efficiency.

, for a given network topology, the energy efficiency can be improved by up to 30% by using our proposed PTC-UT or PTC-USG scheme in combination with the proposed node scheduling algorithm and the interfering-cluster scheduling scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of adaptive power/rate and scheduling control can provide significant energy efficiency improvement in hybrid WSNs, which is especially useful when the network is under heavy traffic load.
the energy efficiency can be significantly improved by using adaptive power/rate controls in combination with time-domain scheduling.
by jointly optimizing the time-domain scheduling, transmission power, and transmission time, we can significantly improve the energy efficiency of a hybrid TDMA-CDMA WSN.
